original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Census the 10640 normalized placements of the two multiplicity-2 sources after an 8-step all-ones interval in a closed length-28 singleton word, and exclude those with no arc-rank-at-least-4 multiplicity matrix.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one new priced connector operation. This package keeps the published singleton alphabet and answers the length-28 all-ones placement split requested by discussion #1166 comment 19537798. It does not add a call or change kappa.
bottleneck_link: A universal length-28 singleton word would show the #5234 floor is sharp and could lower the eight-source query bill. The census removes 2510 normalized all-ones placements from that search under the merged rank bound. No supplier bill is computed.
stop_rule: Stop once the 10640 placements are classified under the rank-at-least-4 test and the cited #7088 budget. Do not search orderings of the surviving matrices, and do not treat a surviving matrix as a universal word.
evidence: Written short-prefix and long-prefix rank bounds (1260 and 42 placements). Exhaustive census: 2510 placements have no rank-at-least-4 matrix and 8130 do; under the cited #7088 budget, 4469 fail and 6171 survive. All 28 label pairs survive both filters. Empty-prefix product agrees. Explicit rank-1 and rank-3 controls.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does any of the 8130 rank-feasible matrices have an ordering whose prefix set is a difference basis of F_2^8?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A yes answer would show that the length-28 floor is compatible with an all-ones interval of length 8.
open_questions.first_step: Order the explicit (0, 1) matrix whose 18 quadruple steps all lie in the final segment.
open_questions.blocked_by: That ordering is unresolved, and a failed search of one matrix would not empty the 8130.

open_questions.question: Do the all-ones distances 10, 12, and 14 have a segment census of the same kind?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The handoff leaves those three anchors open, and together with length 8 they are the shorter circular realizations of all-ones.
open_questions.first_step: Write the repeated-source count vector on an interval of length 10.
open_questions.blocked_by: The identity normalization and the suffix counts both change once a source repeats inside the interval.

open_questions.question: Does a surviving word decide whether the #5234 batch minimum is 538, 540, or 542 queries?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The inherited Gray schedule costs 542 and the proved floor is 538.
open_questions.first_step: Price one universal length-28 word if one is found.
open_questions.blocked_by: No length-28 universal word is known.

claim_type: exhaustive finite census with two written rank bounds
unrun_obligations: No replay of the cited f(7)=24 proof or of the #6966 rank proof.
No re-proof of the open #7088 flat-step budget; the 6171 count assumes it.
No ordering search of the surviving matrices and no claim that a universal length-28 word does not exist.
The all-ones distances 10, 12, and 14 were not enumerated.
No selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, supplier admission, or kappa change.

overlap.novelty_limits: The only remote match is discussion #1166 comment 19537798, the handoff this package answers. Closed PR bodies are covered through local notes and the read predecessors #5234, #6966, #7088, #7015, and #7093, not a full closed-PR body index. No match is a novelty certificate.
